after three years of dealing with the BSOD due to "page fault in nonpaged area) and putting the OS on two different hard drives, re-installing Windows several times, I finally took it into a shop to have it tested, figuring the memory was bad. From what I read online, page fault is either RAM or HDD, and since it persisted through moving the OS to different HDD, I figured it was probably RAM. I wanted to make sure that it was the RAM that was bad, and not something else, before I spent money replacing it.

Both of the HDD have errors. Still waiting on memory results.

Testing your memory is something you can usually do yourself with a little bit of know how. There's a free utility called memtest x86, which you can burn to a CD and boot from. It'll then run a series of tests, and print out any errors that happen. If you get through 2-3 full PASSES (not tests, a whole pass of the tests) without error, you're good.
